doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Trumpet player slaps Sun Ra
summary: A trumpet player in Chicago objected to Sun Ra's space music and slapped him; Allen says he too had a square mind until he learned the spirit.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I see. Did you ever hear people complain or question Sun Ra’s decisions when he wasn’t around?

Yeah. I know there was a night in Chicago, the trumpet player was an accomplished musician, a professional. He wrote music. And he got mad at Sun Ra because Sun Ra was playing his space stuff and all these different systems. And he said, “Oh you can’t do that stuff.” And he’d go — and they were arguing on this stuff and Sun Ra said, “What are you talking about?” And he got mad at Sun Ra and just slapped Sun Ra. Sun Ra turned the other cheek. So he was used to it, being in the square, in a precise — then he could go out of there, it’s not right, you see?

So that’s the way Sun Ra’s music was, they had these ones that had the square mind, just like me. I had that square mind. I could read that stuff and I thought I knew everything. ‘Cause I was a nobody. And then when it comes to the spirit it was a whole different — everything I played is nice but, “It’s not what I want.”
